newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria gives French oil firm operating licence.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria gives French oil firm operating licence.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has given approval to French oil services company Ring Oil International N.V. to operate in the country's downstream sector, a director of the Nigerian unit said.
He said Ring Oil International Nigeria Limited would also be engaged in crude oil lifting.

"The advent of the company is in response to the government's call for private sector investment in the nation's oil and gas industry," said Jeff Ike, director of the Nigerian unit, quoted in the official Daily Times newspaper on Monday.
Ike said Ring Oil International Nigeria Limited is the subsidiary of the French company which would also help to create markets for Nigeria's huge natural gas.
Work is proceeding in the $4 billion liquefied natural gas project in southeastern Bonny aimed at exporting 7.2 billion cubic metres of gas per year from 1999.
Nigeria which has more gas than oil but most of the gas is flared during crude oil production. It wants to end flaring by 2010.
In January, the government announced its 1997 fiscal budget in which it offered numerous incentives to encourage investors to participate in its oil and gas sector.
The government has granted 20 indigenous firms oil prospecting licences to promote local participation in the upstream sector. Some of them are operating in partnership with foreign oil companies.
